title: 雪山神庙
The Temple on the Snow Mountain

name: 冬封碑
The Winter Stele
before: 栈道的最后一块木板钉进了雪里，再往前，天一下子大了：北边、东南、正中，三道雪山白得发蓝，脚下是一片缓缓抬升的高原，风里有酥油和柏烟的味道。坡口立着一块石碑，刻着四个大字「冬不过山」。碑前站着一排护法僧兵，绛红袍子外头套着皮甲，长棍头上包着铁。领头的僧兵说，这是山神的规矩：冬天要过山的人，先过他们。

The last plank of the gallery road is nailed into snow, and beyond it the sky suddenly opens: three snow ranges, north, south-east and in the middle, so white they look blue, and a high plateau rising gently underfoot, with butter and juniper smoke on the wind. At the top of the slope stands a stele carved with four words: NO CROSSING IN WINTER. Before it waits a line of temple warrior-monks, leather armour over their crimson robes, iron caps on their staves. Their leader says it is the Mountain God's rule: whoever wants to cross the mountain in winter must first get past them.
after: 僧兵们揉着胳膊让开了路，领头的反倒向你们合十：「打得过我们，才走得过垭口。走不过的，山会把人留下。」碑的背面有人用刀刻了一行小字，被雪糊住了大半，只看得清前两个字：「护住」。

The monks step aside rubbing their arms, and their leader even bows to you, palms together: 'If you can beat us, you can survive the pass. Those who can't, the mountain keeps.' On the back of the stele someone has cut a line of small characters with a knife. Snow has filled most of it; only the first two words can be read: 'Guard this'.

name: 麝香林
Musk Deer Wood
before: 西边的林子长满了高山柏，雪压弯了枝头。一个小喇嘛被反绑在树上，冻得嘴唇发紫，嘴里还在念经。几个猎麝的弓手张着弓守着他：他把他们下的套子全割了，放跑了三只香獐。怪的是那三只獐子没跑远，就在林边站成一排，眼巴巴地望着他。

The western wood is thick with mountain juniper, its branches bowed under snow. A little monk is tied to a tree, lips blue with cold, still murmuring sutras. A few musk-deer hunters stand guard over him with bows drawn: he cut every snare they had set and let three musk deer go. Oddly, the three deer have not gone far. They stand in a row at the edge of the wood, watching him.
after: 猎户被赶出了林子，香獐这才钻进雪里不见了。小喇嘛叫扎西，是温泉寺的。他背的柏枝捆用一条旧纸带扎着，纸上印着半个「千」字。「这是师父的茶纸，」他说，「师父有一块汉人留下的茶，十年了，每天只尝一口。」

The hunters are chased out of the wood, and only then do the deer slip away into the snow. The little monk is Zhaxi, from the Hot Spring Temple. His bundle of juniper is tied with an old paper band printed with half of the character for 'thousand'. 'That's my master's tea paper,' he says. 'He has a brick of tea a Han man left. Ten years now, and he tastes just one mouthful a day.'

name: 炭窑坪
Kiln Flat
before: 林边一溜土窑，原是烧炭人的，冬天山上的寺庙和帐篷全靠这里的炭过冬。一伙逃兵占了窑，把炭垛围起来卖，一筐炭换一只羊，换不起的人家只好烧牛粪，烟熏得孩子直咳嗽。烧炭的老汉被他们赶去背水，背一趟给一块炭。

A row of earth kilns stands at the edge of the wood. They belong to the charcoal burners, and every temple and tent on the mountain gets through winter on their charcoal. A band of deserters has taken the kilns and fenced off the stacks: one basket of charcoal for one sheep. Families who can't pay burn dung, and their children cough in the smoke. The old charcoal burner has been put to carrying water, one lump of charcoal a trip.
after: 逃兵被打散，窑口又冒起了青烟。老汉说温泉寺的贡布喇嘛十年来每天来要一根炭条，不多不少：「烧一壶水，泡一口茶，够了。」他算过，十年三千六百多根，「这寺里的茶，喝得比炭还省」。

The deserters scatter, and blue smoke rises from the kilns again. The old man says Lama Gonpo of the Hot Spring Temple has come for one stick of charcoal a day for ten years, never more, never less: 'One kettle, one mouthful of tea, that's enough.' He has worked it out: over three thousand six hundred sticks. 'That temple drinks its tea more sparingly than I burn charcoal.'
first: 查抄出逃兵囤的四十袋好炭、一口抢来的铜壶、两张狼皮、一箱硬得能砸核桃的军饼，还有一本赊账簿，记的全是换不起炭的人家，老汉当场把它塞进了窑里。

You seize the deserters' hoard: forty sacks of good charcoal, a stolen copper kettle, two wolf pelts, a crate of army biscuits hard enough to crack walnuts, and a ledger of debts listing every family that couldn't pay. The old man feeds the ledger straight into a kiln.
pass: 每次路过，烧炭的人家都塞给你们一袋刚出窑的炭，裹在毡子里，还热着，袋口埋着几个烤土豆：「上山冷，揣着走。」

Every time you pass, the charcoal families hand you a sack of charcoal fresh from the kiln, wrapped in felt and still warm, with a few roasted potatoes buried at the top: 'It's cold up the mountain. Keep these close.'

name: 分赃坪
Sharing-Out Flat
before: 野地上一伙盗马贼刚干完一票，抢来的马圈在中间，人围着篝火分赃，吵得脸红脖子粗。火边铺着一张羊皮画的地图，画的是一座小寺，寺中间一池水，水边画了个圈，圈里写着两个字：「汉宝」。他们下一票要干的，就是这座寺。

A band of horse thieves has just finished a job. The stolen horses are penned in the middle and the men sit round a fire sharing out the loot, shouting themselves red in the face. By the fire lies a map drawn on sheepskin: a small temple with a pool in the middle, and by the pool a circle with two words inside it: 'HAN TREASURE'. That temple is their next job.
after: 盗马贼被冲散了，马群还给了附近的牧人。羊皮图背面盖着土司管家多吉的印：雇他们去温泉寺取「汉人留下的宝罐」，事成给五十两。扎西看了直跺脚：「哪有什么宝罐，就是一个茶罐！」

The thieves are routed and the horses go back to the herders nearby. On the back of the map is the seal of Dorje, steward to the local chieftain: he hired them to fetch 'the treasure jar the Han man left' from the Hot Spring Temple, fifty taels on delivery. Zhaxi stamps his foot: 'Treasure jar? It's a tea caddy!'

name: 汤钱卡
Bath-Toll Bar
before: 往温泉去的路口横着一根木杆，几个牦牛骑守在杆下，是土司家的税丁，给每个去泡温泉治冻疮的人收「汤钱」：一个人一块酥油，一头牦牛一张皮。几个转山的老人脚上缠着破布，掏不出酥油，只好坐在雪地里等，一等就是一天。

A pole bars the road to the hot spring, and a few yak riders sit beneath it: the chieftain's tax men, taking a 'bath toll' from everyone who comes to soak their frostbite. One lump of butter a person, one hide a yak. A few old pilgrims with rags round their feet have no butter to give, so they sit in the snow and wait, all day long.
after: 税丁被掀下牦牛，木杆劈了当柴。税簿最后一页写着：「温泉寺，欠汤钱十年。屡催，欲以寺中汉茶抵，喇嘛不允，云：茶是借的，不是我的。」老人们一瘸一拐地往温泉去了，扎西走在最前头扶着他们。

The tax men are tipped off their yaks and the pole is split for firewood. The last page of their tax book reads: 'Hot Spring Temple, ten years' toll unpaid. Pressed often; offered to take the temple's Han tea instead. The lama refused, saying: the tea is borrowed, it is not mine.' The old pilgrims limp off towards the spring, Zhaxi in front helping them along.

name: 木碗铺
The Bowl-Maker's
before: 野地里一间木碗铺，墙上挂满了桦木瘤子挖成的碗，油亮亮的，一只好碗能抵一头牛。管家多吉的家丁堵在门口，要老碗匠赶在土司寿辰前做一百只碗，一文不给。老碗匠把刻刀往案上一插，说不做，家丁就把他的徒弟拴在了门柱上。

Out in the open stands a bowl-maker's shop, its walls hung with bowls turned from birch burls, glossy with oil; a good one is worth a yak. Steward Dorje's servants block the door: the old bowl-maker is to make a hundred bowls for the chieftain's birthday, unpaid. He drove his knife into the bench and said no, so they have tied his apprentice to the doorpost.
after: 家丁被赶走，徒弟解了下来，铺子重新开张，老碗匠拿碗换你们车上的货，还附送擦碗的酥油。他记得十年前有个汉人镖头来订过一只碗，只有核桃那么大，带盖：「他说是给寺里的喇嘛，一天尝一口，碗大了就喝多了。」

The servants are driven off, the apprentice untied, and the shop opens again. The old man trades his bowls for your goods and throws in butter for polishing them. He remembers a Han escort chief who ordered a bowl ten years ago, no bigger than a walnut, with a lid: 'He said it was for the lama at the temple. One taste a day. A bigger bowl and he'd drink too much.'

name: 长生茶摊
The Long-Life Tea Stall
before: 林间小路上搭着个棚子，棚下堆着一块块黑乎乎的「茶砖」，招牌上写着「千里号长生茶，喝一口多活一年」。摊主是个白胖的假喇嘛，雇了一帮披着红袍的打手，过路的人不买就不放行。一个老阿爸刚买了一块，啃了一口，崩掉半颗牙。

A shed stands over the woodland path, piled with blackish 'tea bricks' under a sign: QIANLI CARAVAN LONG-LIFE TEA, ONE SIP, ONE MORE YEAR. The stallholder is a plump fake lama with a gang of bruisers in borrowed red robes, and no one passes without buying. An old herdsman has just bought a brick, taken a bite, and broken half a tooth.
after: 打手被打散，「茶砖」掰开一看，是松树皮掺酥油压的。假喇嘛哭着招了：温泉寺的贡布喇嘛九十岁了，天天喝一口汉人的茶，腿脚比谁都利索，山下都传那是长生茶，「我就想沾一点光」。

The bruisers scatter, and the 'tea' turns out to be pine bark pressed with butter. The fake lama confesses in tears: Lama Gonpo at the Hot Spring Temple is ninety, drinks a mouthful of Han tea every day and gets about better than anyone, so the valley says it's long-life tea. 'I only wanted a little of the shine.'

name: 卓玛帐
Drolma's Tent
before: 野地上一顶黑牦牛毛的帐篷，女主人卓玛正跟一伙骑牦牛的邻部汉子对骂：他们趁夜赶走了她二十头牦牛，说她家草场越了界。帐篷门口站着个九岁的男孩，攥着一根抛石绳，冲牦牛骑大喊：「我是陆九！把牛还来！」

A black yak-hair tent stands in the open, and its mistress Drolma is trading insults with a band of yak riders from the next clan: they drove off twenty of her yaks in the night, saying her pasture had crossed the line. A nine-year-old boy stands in the doorway gripping a sling and shouting at the riders: 'I am Lu Jiu! Give our yaks back!'
after: 牦牛赶了回来。卓玛说儿子的名字是照十年前一个汉人起的：那人一个人背着铁匣上山，在她帐里歇了一夜，临走托她每月给温泉寺送一包酥油：「茶要配酥油，喇嘛一个人喝，太苦。」她送了十年，从没断过。

The yaks come home. Drolma says her son is named after a Han man from ten years ago. He was climbing the mountain alone with an iron casket on his back, and rested one night in her tent. As he left he asked her to take a parcel of butter to the Hot Spring Temple every month: 'Tea wants butter. The lama drinks it alone; it'll be too bitter.' She has done it for ten years and never missed a month.

name: 雪狼沟
Snow Wolf Gully
before: 沟口的雪地上全是爪印，一层压一层。雪狼群在沟里安了窝，冬天饿极了就下山，扑牧人的羊，扑转山的人，去年还扑倒了温泉寺的老骡子，骡背上的褡裢被叼进了沟里。头狼的眼睛是灰的，站在高处一动不动地看着你们。

The snow at the mouth of the gully is trodden with paw prints, layer on layer. A snow wolf pack has denned here, and when winter starves them they come down on the herders' sheep and on pilgrims. Last year they brought down the Hot Spring Temple's old mule and dragged its saddlebag into the gully. The lead wolf has grey eyes and stands on a rock above you, perfectly still, watching.
after: 狼群被赶进了深山。可雪狼一窝接一窝地生，雪一厚就又会下来，牧人们只能年年清一回沟。沟里找回了寺里那只褡裢，里头是一本小册子，贡布喇嘛的字，一天一行：「味如故」「略厚」「更醇」……写满了十年。

The pack is driven deep into the mountains. But snow wolves breed litter after litter, and when the snow lies deep they will come again; the herders have to clear the gully every year. In it you find the temple's saddlebag, and inside a little book in Lama Gonpo's hand, one line a day: 'Taste unchanged.' 'A little fuller.' 'Mellower.' Ten years of it.

name: 骨卦台
The Bone-Reading Rock
before: 野地里一块平顶大石，石上摆着一副羊肩胛骨，烧得满是裂纹，是老卦师的卦台。一伙雪山弓手占了台子，逼他算「哪天去温泉寺下手最好」。老卦师闭着眼不肯算，弓手们就把他的卦骨一块块扔进火里。

A great flat-topped rock stands in the open, and on it a sheep's shoulder blade, scorched all over with cracks: the old diviner's reading stone. A band of snow-mountain archers has taken it and wants him to divine 'the best day to hit the Hot Spring Temple'. He keeps his eyes shut and refuses, so they toss his reading bones one by one into the fire.
after: 弓手被赶跑，老卦师从灰里扒出最旧的一块卦骨。他说九年前二月，贡布喇嘛来问过一卦：那天茶尝着是苦的，喇嘛吓坏了。「我烧了骨，纹断成两截：路断了，人还在。第二天，茶又甜了。」他眨眨眼：「其实是头天有个下山的骡夫告诉我的。」

With the archers gone, the old diviner rakes his oldest bone out of the ashes. Nine years ago in the second month, he says, Lama Gonpo came to ask for a reading: the tea had tasted bitter that day, and the lama was frightened. 'I burned the bone and the crack broke in two: the road is broken, the people are alive. Next day the tea was sweet again.' He winks. 'Truth is, a muleteer coming down the mountain had told me the day before.'

name: 驮盐道
The Salt Trail
before: 山脚下的驮盐道，牦牛驮着盐块从北边的盐湖下来，一路往温泉寺和山下的村子送。管家多吉派了一队牦牛骑堵在道上，盐一律截下：谁给温泉寺送盐，就是跟土司作对。盐帮的头人蹲在路边，看着自家的盐块被一块块敲碎。

Along the salt trail at the foot of the mountains, yaks carry blocks of salt down from the northern salt lakes to the Hot Spring Temple and the villages below. Steward Dorje has put a troop of yak riders across the trail to stop every load: anyone who brings salt to the temple is defying the chieftain. The head of the salt carriers squats by the road watching his blocks smashed one by one.
after: 牦牛骑被打退，盐又驮了起来。头人说多吉想饿着温泉寺，逼喇嘛交出那罐茶：「茶里没盐，喝着跟水一样，他以为喇嘛就会松口。」他往你们车上放了一块最白的盐：「替我捎给喇嘛。十年前那个汉人，在这条道上也给过我们一块茶。」

The riders are beaten back and the salt moves again. Dorje wanted to starve the temple into handing over the tea, the headman says: 'Tea without salt tastes like water. He thought the lama would give in.' He puts his whitest block in your cart: 'Take that to the lama for me. That Han man ten years ago gave us a piece of tea on this very trail.'

name: 热水河
Warm River
before: 野地里一条小河冒着白汽，两岸积雪，河面却一冰不结，几百只赤麻鸭挤在水上过冬。一伙弓手蹲在岸边的石头后面，一箭一只，射了往土司府里送。扎西急得直掉眼泪：这些鸭子是温泉寺的客人，每年冬天都来。

A little river steams through the open country. Snow lies deep on both banks, but the water never freezes, and hundreds of ruddy shelducks crowd onto it for the winter. A band of archers crouches behind the boulders on the bank, one arrow, one duck, for the chieftain's kitchen. Zhaxi is nearly in tears: the ducks are the Hot Spring Temple's guests and come every winter.
after: 弓手被撵走，鸭子又落回了水上。扎西说河是从寺里的温泉流出来的：「泉水从很深的地底下上来，地底下热，所以冬天也不冻。」十年前那个汉人就是顺着这条不冻的河摸上来的：「他说，跟着热水走，就找得到有人的地方。」

The archers are chased off and the ducks settle back on the water. The river runs out of the temple's hot spring, Zhaxi says: 'The water comes up from very deep under the ground, and it's hot down there, so it doesn't freeze even in winter.' The Han man ten years ago found the temple by following this unfrozen river: 'He said, follow the warm water and you'll find people.'

name: 温泉寺
Hot Spring Temple
before: 温泉寺不大，几间白墙小殿围着一池冒热气的泉水，雪落进池里就没了。管家多吉带着弓手把寺门堵了，在门外喊话：交出汉人的宝罐，就撤兵。池边坐着贡布喇嘛，九十岁，眉毛全白，膝上放着一只核桃大的木碗，碗里只有几片茶叶。他没有看门外，只看着碗。

The Hot Spring Temple is small: a few white-walled shrines round a steaming pool, where falling snow vanishes the moment it touches the water. Steward Dorje and his archers have the gate blocked and shout through it: hand over the Han man's treasure jar and they'll leave. By the pool sits Lama Gonpo, ninety years old, his eyebrows white, a walnut-sized wooden bowl on his knee with a few tea leaves in it. He doesn't look at the gate. He looks at the bowl.
after:
弓手们退下山去了。贡布喇嘛用小碗泡了一口茶，请你们每人尝一点：一块黑茶，越放越醇。十年前的冬天，一个背铁匣的汉人在池里泡了三天冻伤的脚，临走留下这块茶：「每天替我尝一口。味不变，我们就都还在。」

茶罐里，只剩指甲盖大的一撮了。

The archers retreat down the mountain. Lama Gonpo brews one mouthful in the little bowl and gives each of you a taste: a dark tea that has only grown mellower with the years. Ten winters ago, he says, a Han man with an iron casket soaked his frostbitten feet in this pool for three days, and left this tea when he went: 'Taste it once a day for me. While the taste holds, we're all still alive.'

In the caddy there is only a pinch left, the size of a fingernail.

name: 土司冰窖
The Chieftain's Ice Cellar
before: 野地尽头是土司家的冰窖，半埋在地下，门口的石狮子挂着冰溜子。多吉手下最精的家兵守在这里，刀手、弓手、骑兵一样不缺，比堵寺门的那伙凶得多。扎西说寺里这几年丢的东西，十有八九藏在这里：经卷、铜铃，还有一封信。

At the end of the open ground lies the chieftain's ice cellar, half sunk in the earth, icicles hanging from the stone lions at its door. Dorje's best men guard it, swordsmen, archers and riders, much fiercer than the lot at the temple gate. Zhaxi says most of what the temple has lost in recent years is in there: scriptures, a bronze bell, and a letter.
after: 家兵被打退，冰窖门开了，寒气扑面。冰块中间冻着寺里丢的铜铃和经卷，还有一封六年前从山上捎下来、被多吉截住的信，陆字落款：「贡布师父：茶若喝到了底，就是后来的人到了。请他们上山一趟。」扎西把信揣进怀里，一路小跑回寺。

The guards fall back and the cellar door opens on a breath of cold. Frozen among the ice blocks are the temple's bell and scriptures, and a letter sent down from the mountain six years ago that Dorje intercepted, signed with the character Lu: 'Master Gonpo: if the tea runs out, it means those who come after have arrived. Please send them up the mountain.' Zhaxi tucks it inside his robe and runs all the way back to the temple.

name: 告示坡
Proclamation Slope
before: 山脚下，多吉的家兵摆开了阵势，前排举盾，后排拉弓，两边是牦牛骑。多吉站在土堆上念土司的告示，念一句，家兵齐喊一声「遵命」。告示太长，念到一半，后排喊早了，前排喊晚了，多吉气得跺脚，只好从头再念。他念到第三遍的时候，你们已经冲到了跟前。

At the foot of the mountains Dorje's men are drawn up: shields in front, bows behind, yak riders on the wings. Dorje stands on a mound reading out the chieftain's proclamation, and after every line his men roar 'We obey!' But it's a long proclamation, and halfway through the back rank shouts too early and the front rank too late, so Dorje stamps his foot and starts again. He is on his third reading when you reach him.
after: 家兵四散，多吉被从土堆上拽了下来，抱着告示直嚷：「我还没念完！」告示最后一句是土司的原话：「取汉茶，献我延寿。」多吉哭丧着脸说土司老了，怕死，他就想讨个好，「我哪知道，那就是一撮茶叶」。

The men scatter and Dorje is hauled off his mound, clutching the proclamation and wailing, 'I hadn't finished!' Its last line is in the chieftain's own words: 'Bring me the Han tea, that I may live longer.' The chieftain is old and afraid of dying, Dorje says miserably, and he only wanted to please him. 'How was I to know it was a pinch of tea leaves?'

name: 磕头道
The Prostration Path
before: 山脚的转山道上，一个老人在磕长头：三步一拜，五体投地，额头磕出了一块硬茧。道口被一伙「护法」拦住了，穿着红袍却戴着狼皮帽，说转山要交功德钱，一圈一两银子，交不起的往回走。老人不交也不回头，就趴在雪地里，一下一下地磕。他们最精的人手都压在这里，刀、弓、马，一样不少。

On the pilgrim circuit at the mountain's foot an old man is making full prostrations: three steps, then down flat on the ground, a hard callus on his forehead. The way ahead is blocked by a band of 'temple guardians' in red robes but wolfskin hats, demanding a merit fee of one tael a circuit; those who can't pay turn back. The old man neither pays nor turns. He lies in the snow and keeps on bowing. They have their best men here, blades, bows and horses.
after: 假护法被打散了。老人爬起来冲你们笑，掉了两颗门牙。他叫阿旺，要转十三圈，这是第十二圈。他怀里揣着一片干茶叶，是贡布喇嘛十年前给的：「喇嘛说，转完十三圈再尝，就知道等人是什么滋味。」他没说为谁转，只说转完了，要去「交一样东西」。

The false guardians are scattered. The old man gets up and grins at you, two front teeth missing. He is Awang, and he means to walk thirteen circuits; this is his twelfth. Inside his coat he keeps one dry tea leaf Lama Gonpo gave him ten years ago: 'The lama said, taste it when you've done thirteen, and you'll know what waiting for someone tastes like.' He won't say who he walks for, only that when he's done he has 'something to hand back'.

name: 土司官寨
The Chieftain's Keep
before: 野地上一座石砌的官寨，碉楼七层，窗口小得只容一支箭。管家多吉跑了，寨里的家丁还守着他留下的令：汉人一个不许进。可碉楼顶上，老土司扒着窗口，一个劲地朝你们招手，被家丁一次次拉回去。

A stone keep rises from the open ground, seven storeys high, its windows barely wide enough for an arrow. Steward Dorje has fled, but the keep's men still follow his last order: no Han gets in. Yet at the top of the tower the old chieftain hangs out of a window, waving at you again and again, and his men keep pulling him back inside.
after: 家丁被打散，老土司拄着拐下了楼。他不是要长生，是要赔罪：十年前那个雪夜，背铁匣的汉人在寨门口敲了半夜，他没开门。「第二天我派人去找，雪地里只有一行脚印，往温泉去了。」他想尝一口那块茶，「就当是请他进了门」。

With the guards scattered, the old chieftain comes down on his stick. He never wanted to live forever; he wants to make amends. Ten years ago on a night of snow, the Han man with the iron casket knocked at his gate half the night, and he didn't open it. 'Next day I sent men to look, and there was one line of footprints in the snow, heading for the hot spring.' He wants a taste of that tea, 'as if I'd let him in after all'.

name: 热水塘集
Hot Pool Fair
before: 温泉下游的热水塘是方圆百里唯一冬天不封的集市：牧人背来河里淘的金沙，换山下的石料，修羊圈，砌浴池。如今集口被一伙雪山弓手占着，他们自称「秤主」，金沙过秤一律七折，石料要另交过路钱。去年发大水冲垮了浴池，到现在也没人修得起。

Below the hot spring lies Hot Pool, the only market for a hundred miles that stays open in winter: herders bring gold dust washed from the river and trade it for stone from the valleys to build pens and line the bathing pools. Now a band of snow-mountain archers holds the entrance. They call themselves the Masters of the Scales: all gold dust weighed at seventy parts in a hundred, a toll on every load of stone. Last year's flood broke the bathing pools, and no one has been able to afford the repair since.
after:
「秤主」被赶跑，官秤重新挂上，石换金的买卖开了张，牧人们当天就把浴池的墙垒起了一角。

贡布喇嘛十年来头一回下山赶集，捧着茶罐，把最后那一撮分出一点，泡给老土司尝了。老土司喝完，掉了眼泪。喇嘛把罐盖一扣：「剩下的，带上山去。」他要跟你们一起走。扎西急得直拽他袖子：师父九十岁了。

The Masters of the Scales are driven off, the market scales hung up again, and the trade of stone for gold opens. By evening the herders have rebuilt a corner of the bathing pool wall.

For the first time in ten years Lama Gonpo comes down to the fair. He opens the caddy, takes a few leaves from the last pinch, and brews them for the old chieftain, who weeps as he drinks. Then the lama snaps the lid shut: 'The rest goes up the mountain.' He means to come with you. Zhaxi tugs frantically at his sleeve. His master is ninety.

name: 雪埋营
The Buried Camp
before: 山脚下有一片塌下去的雪坡，九年前一场雪崩把一整个牧人的冬营埋在了底下。如今一伙扒坟的外来客在这里挖，刀手开路，弓手放哨，骑手驮货，专挖死人身上的银饰和珊瑚。扎西站在坡下，一句话也不说。师父告诉过他，他就是在这里被挖出来的。

At the foot of the mountains lies a slumped slope of snow. Nine years ago an avalanche buried a whole herders' winter camp beneath it. Now a gang of outsiders is digging here, blades in front, bows on watch, riders to carry the spoil, after the silver and coral on the dead. Zhaxi stands at the bottom of the slope and says nothing. His master told him this is where he was dug out.
after: 扒坟客被打跑了，挖开的坑一个个重新填上。坡下露出半只木摇篮，摇篮把手上拴着一只铜铃。扎西把铃解下来，摇了摇，铃声闷闷的。贡布喇嘛说，那年整个冬营只活下来一个娃娃，「是一个戴面具的人从雪里刨出来的，刨了一天一夜」。

The grave-robbers are chased off and their pits filled in again. At the foot of the slope half a wooden cradle shows through, a little bronze bell tied to its handle. Zhaxi unties the bell and shakes it; it rings dully. That winter, Lama Gonpo says, only one baby lived out of the whole camp: 'A man in a mask dug him out of the snow. He dug for a day and a night.'

name: 草场界桩
The Boundary Posts
before: 野地上一排新钉的界桩，把雪埋营留下的草场圈了进去。一个大牧主的护院守着界桩，谁的牛羊过界就扣下。扎西的老阿爸要是还在，这片草场本该是他家的。贡布喇嘛拄着拐走到界桩前，护院们举起了刀，又不敢真砍一个九十岁的喇嘛，只好喊你们来评理。

A row of newly driven boundary posts cuts across the open ground, fencing in the pasture the buried camp left behind. A great herd-owner's guards stand over them and seize any beast that strays across. Had Zhaxi's father lived, this pasture would have been his. Lama Gonpo hobbles up to the posts on his stick; the guards raise their blades but dare not really strike a ninety-year-old lama, so they shout for you to settle it.
after: 护院被打散，界桩拔了。牧主家最老的牧人跑来说，雪崩那夜他就在坡上：一个戴面具的人在雪里刨了一天一夜，手刨出了血，最后抱出一个娃娃，揣在怀里往温泉寺走了，一句话没说。「那人身上，有一股茶味。」

The guards are scattered and the posts pulled up. The herd-owner's oldest herdsman comes running: he was on the slope the night of the avalanche. A man in a mask dug in the snow for a day and a night until his hands bled, and at last lifted out a baby, tucked it inside his coat and walked off towards the Hot Spring Temple without a word. 'He smelled of tea.'

name: 毡匠院
The Felt-Maker's Yard
before: 野地里一个擀毡的院子，院里晾满了白毡。一伙赌徒占了院子当赌场，把毡子铺在地上掷骰子，烟锅烫出一个个窟窿。扎西怀里一直揣着一块旧毡，是他当年被裹着的那块，想请老毡匠认一认，赌徒们嫌他碍事，一把把他推进了雪堆。

Out in the open is a felt-maker's yard hung with white felts. A gang of gamblers has made it their gambling den, rolling dice on felts spread on the ground and burning holes in them with their pipes. Zhaxi has always kept an old piece of felt inside his robe, the one he was wrapped in as a baby, and wants the old felt-maker to look at it. The gamblers find him in the way and shove him into a snowdrift.
after: 赌徒被轰了出去。老毡匠捏着那块旧毡看了半天：毡是藏地的毡，可四角的绳结不是。「这叫镖扣，汉人走镖的才这么打，越拽越紧，摔下山崖也散不开。」他把毡还给扎西：「裹你的人，是个走镖的。」

The gamblers are thrown out. The old felt-maker turns the old felt over in his hands for a long time. The felt is local, but the knots at its four corners are not. 'That's an escort's knot. Only Han escort men tie it that way; the harder you pull, the tighter it holds, and it won't come loose even if you fall off a cliff.' He hands it back to Zhaxi: 'Whoever wrapped you was an escort man.'

name: 石阶垭
Stone Stair Col
before: 山脚上山的路在这里变成一道石阶，一千多级，是历代转山人一块块垒的。一伙牦牛骑横在阶下，是被赶走的那个大牧主雇来出气的，扬言谁也别想上山。贡布喇嘛已经走了三天，气喘得像风箱，扶着扎西的肩膀，看着石阶，又看了看你们。

Here the mountain road turns into a stone stair of more than a thousand steps, laid stone by stone by generations of pilgrims. A troop of yak riders sits across the bottom, hired by the herd-owner you drove off to take out his temper: no one goes up today. Lama Gonpo has been walking for three days and his breath wheezes like a bellows. He leans on Zhaxi's shoulder, looks at the stair, then at you.
after: 牦牛骑被赶下了坡。贡布喇嘛在第一级石阶上坐下来，坐了很久，最后笑了：「上不去了。我在这里等着就好，十年都等了。」他让扎西把炉子支起来，用那根炭条，烧最后一壶水。

The yak riders are driven down the slope. Lama Gonpo sits down on the first step and stays there a long while. At last he smiles: 'I can't go up. I'll wait here, that's fine. I've waited ten years.' He has Zhaxi set up the little stove and light the one stick of charcoal to boil the last kettle of water.

name: 望庙台
Temple-View Terrace
before: 石阶边一块平台，天晴的时候，能望见东边雪山上那座神庙的金顶，一点点亮。平台上的风马旗被一伙雪山弓手割下来烤火，他们是来劫路的，看见喇嘛的茶炉，以为炉子里煮的是金子，一齐把箭对准了你们。

Beside the stair is a terrace, and on a clear day you can see the golden roof of the temple on the eastern snow mountain from it, one small point of light. A band of snow-mountain archers has cut down the prayer flags here to feed their fire. They have come to rob the road, and when they see the lama's tea stove they think there's gold boiling in it, and all of them turn their arrows on you.
after:
弓手被打散了。水开了，贡布喇嘛把最后一撮茶分成两半：一半泡了，分着喝；一半用纸包好，交到你们手里：「带给他。告诉他味没变，扎西长大了。」

扎西攥着铜铃说，他认得这股味道：很小的时候，在一个很冷的地方，有人把他揣在怀里，怀里就是这个味道。

The archers are scattered. The water boils, and Lama Gonpo divides the last pinch in two. Half he brews, and all of you share it. The other half he wraps in paper and puts in your hands: 'Take it to him. Tell him the taste never changed, and Zhaxi has grown up.'

Gripping the little bronze bell, Zhaxi says he knows this smell. When he was very small, somewhere very cold, someone held him inside his coat, and that coat smelled just like this.

name: 旧号衣
The Old Uniforms
before: 野地上一大伙劫道的，穿着褪了色的边军号衣，补丁摞补丁，刀手、弓手、骑手居然还排得有模有样。他们抢了一支牧人的驮队，正要散伙分东西。你们的领队随口喊了一声「列队！」，对面竟有一半人一激灵，啪地站直了。

A large band of highwaymen is out on the open ground, wearing faded frontier-army coats, patch on patch, swordsmen, archers and riders drawn up in surprisingly good order. They have just robbed a herders' pack train and are about to split the goods. Your leader barks 'Fall in!' without thinking, and half of them jump and snap to attention.
after: 劫道的被打散，驮队还给了牧人。站直的那几个老汉红着脸说，他们原是碎石营的兵：十年前朝廷一道旨意撤了营，五百人就地遣散，没了饷，只好干这个。问营将去了哪里，他们互相看看：「交了甲，不知去向。」

The highwaymen are scattered and the pack train returned to the herders. The old men who stood to attention say, red-faced, that they were soldiers of the Gravel Camp. Ten years ago an edict from the court disbanded the camp; five hundred men were turned loose where they stood, with no pay, and this was all that was left. Where did their commander go? They look at each other: 'He handed in his armour. Nobody knows where he went.'

name: 更鼓墩
The Drum Mound
before: 野地里一座土墩，墩上架着一面牛皮大鼓，一个聋了的老兵守着它，日头到哪儿，他就敲到哪儿，一个时辰一通鼓，十年没误过。附近牧主家的打手嫌鼓声吓着了牦牛，带着棍棒来砸鼓。老兵张开胳膊挡在鼓前，他听不见骂声，只看得见棍子。

A mound of earth stands in the open, and on it a great oxhide drum, kept by an old deaf soldier who beats the hours by the sun, one roll every two hours, and hasn't missed one in ten years. The local herd-owner's bullies say the drum frightens the yaks, and have come with clubs to smash it. The old soldier spreads his arms in front of it. He can't hear their curses; he can only see their clubs.
after: 打手被赶走了，老兵比划着跟你们讲：他最后一回奉命擂的鼓是「撤营」。那天夜里营将一个人骑马出了营，往雪山去了，第二天走着回来，马没了，甲也没了。「营没撤完，」老兵说，「营将还没走，我就不走。」

With the bullies gone, the old soldier tells you in signs: the last order he drummed was 'Strike camp'. That night the commander rode out alone towards the snow mountains, and came back on foot next day, with no horse and no armour. 'The camp isn't struck,' the old soldier says. 'The commander hasn't left, so neither have I.'

name: 旧箭场
The Old Butts
before: 野地上一片旧箭场，一排木靶桩早被风沙打得发白。一伙雪山弓手在这里操练，是盐枭花钱雇的，准备开春押盐过山。他们拿过路人当靶子玩，射掉人的帽子算一分，射穿袖子算两分。一个放羊的孩子顶着一只破锅，吓得不敢动。

An old archery ground lies in the open, its row of target posts long bleached by wind and grit. A company of snow-mountain archers trains here, hired by salt smugglers to guard their loads over the pass in spring. They use passers-by as targets for fun: a hat shot off scores one, a sleeve pinned scores two. A shepherd boy stands frozen with a battered pot on his head.
after: 弓手被赶跑，孩子扔下锅就跑了。最边上一根靶桩上，刀刻着一行字，被风磨得只剩浅浅的痕：「丁未冬，奉旨撤营，封山。霍。」老兵们说，那是营将亲手刻的：旨意里写的是封山，一个人也不许放过去。

The archers are driven off and the boy drops the pot and runs. On the last target post a line has been cut with a knife, worn by the wind to the faintest trace: 'Winter, Dingwei year. By edict: strike camp, close the mountain. Huo.' The old soldiers say the commander carved it himself. The edict said close the mountain: let no one through.

name: 老马厩
The Old Stables
before: 野地上一排土墙马厩，是碎石营当年的马营，如今住着一伙偷牦牛的牦牛骑，厩里拴满了别人家的牛，牛角上的记号都被锯掉了。看马厩的老马夫被他们留下来喂牛，一天给一碗糌粑，老马夫偷偷把自己的那碗也喂了牛。

A row of mud-walled stables stands in the open: the Gravel Camp's old horse lines, now home to a gang of yak rustlers whose stalls are full of other people's yaks with the brand marks sawn off their horns. The old groom has been kept on to feed them for one bowl of tsampa a day, and he secretly feeds his own bowl to the yaks too.
after: 牦牛骑被赶走，牛都还给了失主。老马夫指着最里头一间厩说，十年前腊月里，营将在这里关过一个人：一个背铁匣子的汉人，要过山。「旨意说封山，营将就把他关在这儿。」老马夫说，那人一点也不闹，靠着墙，抱着匣子，就那么坐着。

The rustlers are driven out and the yaks returned to their owners. The old groom points to the innermost stall. Ten years ago in the twelfth month, he says, the commander shut a man in there: a Han man with an iron casket on his back, who wanted to cross the mountain. 'The edict said close the mountain, so the commander locked him up here.' The man made no fuss at all, the groom says. He just sat against the wall with the casket in his arms.

name: 夹生面棚
The Half-Cooked Noodle Shed
before: 碎石滩上一个面棚，掌勺的胖伙夫原是碎石营的厨子。一伙弓手吃完面不给钱，说他的面是夹生的，砸了他两口锅。胖伙夫气得满脸通红：在山下，他的面是全营最好的；一上了这滩，面怎么煮都硬，他自己也想不通。

On the gravel flats stands a noodle shed, and its fat cook was once the Gravel Camp's cook. A band of archers has eaten without paying, saying his noodles are half raw, and smashed two of his pots. The fat cook is purple with rage: down in the valley his noodles were the best in the camp, but up on these flats they come out hard however he boils them, and he can't work out why.
after: 弓手被打跑了。你们里头有人点破：地方越高，气越薄，水不到那么烫就开了，面自然煮不透。胖伙夫拿平石头死死压住锅盖，憋住了气，面果然软了。他说当年关在马厩里的汉人吃过他的面，说：「我不是来闯关的，是来等人的。」那一夜，营将陪他坐到天亮。

The archers are chased off. One of your people explains it: the higher you go, the thinner the air, so water boils before it gets as hot, and the noodles never cook through. The fat cook weighs his pot lid down hard with a flat stone to keep the steam in, and sure enough the noodles come out soft. The Han man locked in the stables ate his noodles once, he says, and told him: 'I'm not here to force the pass. I'm here to wait for people.' That night the commander sat up with him till dawn.

name: 鞍褥坡
Saddlecloth Slope
before: 野地坡上一伙牦牛骑在晒太阳，他们的头领屁股底下垫着一块破旧的大旗当鞍褥，旗上的字被磨得模糊，边上的流苏都秃了。老兵们远远一看就红了眼：那是碎石营的营旗。头领听说他们想要，故意在旗上啐了一口。

A troop of yak riders is lazing in the sun on an open slope, and their leader sits on a big tattered banner folded as a saddlecloth, its characters worn faint, its fringe bald. The old soldiers see it from afar and their eyes go red: it is the Gravel Camp's banner. When the leader hears they want it, he spits on it on purpose.
after: 牦牛骑被打下了坡，营旗从鞍上揭了下来。老兵们拍掉灰，把旗展开，正中一个斗大的「霍」字，旁边一行小字：「碎石营，戍此山十二年」。几个老兵把旗杆竖起来，旗一升起，坡下居然有放牧的老汉朝着它敬了个礼。

The riders are driven off the slope and the banner is pulled from the saddle. The old soldiers beat out the dust and spread it: in the middle one great character, Huo, and beside it a line of small ones: 'Gravel Camp, twelve years on guard at this mountain.' They raise it on a pole, and as it goes up an old herdsman down the slope actually salutes it.

name: 空粮仓
The Empty Granary
before: 野地里碎石营的旧粮仓，一伙盐枭把它改成了盐库，仓里码满了私盐，门口站着刀手。他们怕人看见，把仓墙上的字全拿泥糊上了。看仓的老兵说墙上记的是营里最后一个冬天的账，糊了，就再没人知道那年冬天的事了。

The Gravel Camp's old granary stands in the open. Salt smugglers have turned it into a salt store, stacked with contraband, with swordsmen at the door. Afraid of being seen, they have plastered over every mark on the walls. The old soldier who kept the granary says the walls held the camp's accounts for its last winter, and with them plastered over, no one will ever know what happened that winter.
after: 盐枭被赶走，私盐充了公，你们拿水把墙上的泥一点点洗掉。最后一行炭字写着：「腊月廿三，开马厩，放一人上山。粮二斗，炭十斤，营将自出。」老兵们看了半天，谁也没说话。营将抗了旨。

The smugglers are driven off and their salt confiscated, and you wash the mud from the walls bit by bit. The last line, in charcoal, reads: 'Twelfth month, twenty-third day. Stables opened, one man let up the mountain. Grain two pecks, charcoal ten catties, paid by the commander himself.' The old soldiers stare at it a long time, and none of them speaks. Their commander had defied the edict.
